key_insight: A stacking machine learning model using pre-operative clinical features can predict Mohs micrographic surgery cases likely to require 13 or more tissue sections with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinics plan operating time, allocate resources, and counsel patients before surgery.
method: Analysed 408 consecutive Mohs procedures with 16 pre-operative clinical variables.
Compared 30 machine learning algorithms, including ensemble models, gradient boosting, neural networks, SVMs, and traditional classifiers.
Used 5-fold stratified cross-validation, independent test evaluation, and SHAP to identify key predictors.
evidence_signal: The stacking ensemble achieved the best performance, with cross-validation AUC 0.891 and test AUC 0.884.
watch_item: The model needs external validation in multi-centre cohorts before it can be relied on across different patient populations and practice settings.
paper_title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting 13 or More Sections in Mohs Micrographic Surgery
